title: The Man Who Sold Wednesdays
hook: Dottie's diner has receipts for meals nobody remembers ordering, all dated Wednesday, including one from a man who has been dead for nine years.
truth: An alien chronology accountant is correcting a mistaken interstellar ledger by repossessing small pieces of Cedar Crossing's calendar.

monster.name: The Chronology Accountant
monster.instinct: To balance temporal accounts by filing people, places, and events under the wrong dates.

countdown.label: Wrong Receipts
countdown.text: Dottie's register prints breakfast orders dated next Wednesday.

countdown.label: Missing Hour
countdown.text: The noon rush lasts six minutes for some people and ninety minutes for others.

countdown.label: Road Loop
countdown.text: County Road 9 traps three cars between mile markers for most of an afternoon.

countdown.label: Dead Customer
countdown.text: A dead regular sits in his old booth and complains that the coffee is late.

countdown.label: Public Ledger
countdown.text: Names appear on the civic hall agenda under dates that have not happened yet.

countdown.label: Calendar Seizure
countdown.text: The accountant repossesses every Wednesday in town until the ledger is corrected.

clues.text: Receipt ink glows under the same blue light seen over Miller's Field.
The dead customer leaves exact change plus a coin stamped with three moons.
Analog clocks disagree only after someone signs a receipt.
The trapped mile is exactly 1.609 times too long, as if a unit conversion went badly.
A purple stamp on the civic agenda translates roughly as unpaid local interval.
A receipt left unsigned remains anchored in the correct day.

keeperHints: Make time loss feel mundane at first: cold fries, repeated greetings, missed appointments.
The accountant should be precise, courteous, and terrifyingly unwilling to understand context.
Use receipts and public records as strong concrete evidence.
revealPolicy: Reveal the alien bureaucracy through paperwork and timing errors before showing the accountant directly.
automationSafety: Do not erase major player history without explicit approval.
Keep time confusion legible enough for investigation.
